title: NRI EPF Withdrawal: Understanding Taxability and Avoiding Extra Tax
description: Your Employees' Provident Fund (EPF) withdrawal becomes fully tax-exempt in India if you complete five years of continuous service, irrespective of your NRI s.

faq.q: ### Is EPF withdrawal always tax-free for NRIs?
faq.a: No, EPF withdrawal is tax-free in India for NRIs only if you have completed five years of continuous service. If withdrawn before five years, it becomes taxable.

faq.q: ### What is the TDS rate on EPF withdrawal for NRIs if service is less than 5 years?
faq.a: If your PAN is linked, TDS is 10%. If PAN is not linked, TDS is 30% (plus surcharge and cess) for amounts over ₹50,000.

faq.q: ### Can NRIs submit Form 15G or 15H to avoid TDS on EPF?
faq.a: No, Forms 15G and 15H are exclusively for resident Indians and cannot be submitted by NRIs.

faq.q: ### How can an NRI reduce TDS on EPF withdrawal?
faq.a: NRIs can apply for a lower or nil TDS certificate (Form 13) under Section 197 of the Income Tax Act if their actual tax liability is lower. Benefits under Double Taxation Avoidance Agreements (DTAA) may also apply.

faq.q: ### Does interest earned on EPF after becoming an NRI become taxable?
faq.a: Yes, any interest accrued on your EPF balance from the last date of your employment in India until the actual withdrawal date is fully taxable.

faq.q: ### Can NRIs continue contributing to their EPF account?
faq.a: No, once you become an NRI, you are no longer eligible to contribute to your EPF account.

faq.q: ### What happens if I don't withdraw my EPF as an NRI?
faq.a: Your EPF account remains active and continues to earn interest until withdrawal. However, interest earned after the last date of employment becomes taxable.

based_on.title: Moving abroad? Here's when your EPF withdrawal becomes taxable and how NRIs can avoid paying extra tax
